conventions.convention: Minkowski signature is (−+++); x⁰=ct and all four coordinates have units metres. The phase is p∘x=ωμx⁰−k·x=−η(p,x).
For positive rest mass, μ=m_rest,SI c/ℏ and ωμ(k)=sqrt(|k|²+μ²) have units inverse metres; physical energy and momentum are ℏcωμ and ℏk.
c, h and the SI elementary charge have exact defining values; μ₀ is experimentally determined. Normalized charge is q_n=q_SI sqrt(μ₀c/ℏ), and α=e_n²/(4π) receives no exact numerical value.
S/ℏ=∫L_nat d⁴x and L_SI=ℏc L_nat. Scalar, Dirac and photon-potential engineering length degrees are −1, −3/2 and −1; these are not asserted interacting scaling dimensions.
The effective Clifford metric is −η: {γᵃ,γᵇ}=−2ηᵃᵇI₄, β=γ⁰, αⁱ=βγⁱ and barψ=ψ†β. Minimal coupling uses Dμ=∂μ−iq_n aμ.

The root Hilbert pairing is linear in its first variable. A free-field pairing linear in its second variable is converted by ⟨u,v⟩_FF=(v,u)_root. Weak operator-valued distributions require matrix-element continuity on a specified common dense complex-linear domain and supply no pointwise products.
The Schrödinger convention is U(t)=exp(−itH/ℏ), with time in seconds and H in joules. Heisenberg conjugation has domain {ξ:U(t)ξ∈D(O)}.

Born probabilities require an actually constructed density state and normalized finite bounded Kraus instrument, with Countable Choice for the cited normalization theorem. Conditional normalization is assigned only at strictly positive outcome probability.

The two-level space uses coordinates indexed 0 and 1 and pairing x₀ conjugate(y₀)+x₁ conjugate(y₁). Factorials start at 0!=1; numerical g⁰=1 includes g=0. The convergence radius is the supremum of radii whose open disks consist entirely of convergence points.

load_bearing.statement: For an explicitly selected model with actually constructed density state and normalized finite bounded Kraus instrument, adopt p_a(t)=tr(J_a(ρ_t))=tr(ρ_tE_a) as its outcome probability. Assume Countable Choice for the normalization supplier. At positive probability adopt J_a(ρ_t)/p_a(t) as the conditional state; at zero probability assign no normalized update. Dynamics and operator domains must separately be constructed; formal coefficients and agreement with data supply no missing construction.

A unit and domain dictionary for selected quantum-field model data in four-dimensional Minkowski length coordinates. It declares engineering normalizations and conventions only; it constructs no field representation, QED dynamics, continuum limit, apparatus, or empirical result.

alerts.finding: The Statement defines projective measurements by self-adjoint idempotent, mutually orthogonal P_a summing to I, then says: “Equivalently, the one-Kraus-per-outcome data M_{a,1}=P_a form a normalized finite instrument”. The reverse implication is false without retaining the projection hypotheses. For example P₁=P₂=I/√2 gives a normalized one-Kraus-per-outcome instrument because P₁*P₁+P₂*P₂=I, but neither operator is idempotent. The cited finite-instrument definition requires only Kraus normalization. The subsequent proof uses the explicitly stated projection hypotheses, so this finding concerns the overstrong equivalence in the Statement.

seams_checked.note: The postulate preserves the nonzero complex Hilbert space, density state, finite bounded Kraus normalization and Countable Choice hypotheses. It preserves the strictly positive-probability update boundary and explicitly distinguishes the draft mathematical identity from physical adoption and apparatus realization.

Actual uses of the unit dictionary and Born postulate retain constructed finite states and instruments, an explicit preparation/evolution adoption, and the distinction between exact probabilities and truncation-derived squares. The separate false projective-instrument equivalence is routed as an item alert.

The free-model adoption preserves length coordinates, phase, Clifford signs, engineering dimensions and SI energy/momentum conversions. It explicitly supplies a separate massless branch rather than attributing μ=0 to the dictionary's positive-rest-mass definition. Measurement interpretation remains conditional on constructed states and instruments.

The finite-regulator model explicitly supplies its dimensionless coordinates and positive joule-valued energy scale. Physical time is converted by E_*τ/ℏ, matching the Schrödinger convention. Canonical probabilities use an actually constructed density and normalized finite instrument; no continuum or empirical conclusion is inferred.
